method: Rendered every page of the three booklets with music_pages.py render at 110 dpi (listening 1-16, composing 1-16, elective 1-8) and read every ask page in full; zoomed with PyMuPDF clips at 250-800 dpi on each question block and every glyph in doubt: the capitals the text layer stores in lower case (TWICE on listening p2; ONE in Q1 Excerpt 1(ii)/(iii), Excerpt 3(i), Q2(i)/(iii)/(iv), Q5 A Excerpt 3(ii); TWO in Q5 A Excerpt 3(iii); THREE/FIVE/THREE in elective Q2/Q3/Q4(a)) and the words printed in lower case ("Write one bar" in Q5 A Excerpt 1(ii), "Answer one of the following" in Q5 B, printed bold lower case; "three" in elective Q4(b)); hyphen vs en dash (16-bar in the listening Excerpt 1 heading and composing Q3, 16–bar in composing Q1, Bars 1–8 / 9–16 / 1–15 and lines 1–3 / 4–5 en dashes); curly apostrophes in When I’m Sixty-four (lead-in, lyric line 6, Q3(v)); the absence of a full stop after the bold headings Excerpt 1 / Excerpt 2 / Excerpt 3 in Q5 A; accents in Seán Ó Riada and their absence in Saint-Saens; every bullet at the left margin of each lead-in (Q2 prints a bullet before "An outline score ..."; Q5 A prints none); the superscript 1s and the closing full stop in AA¹BB¹. (800 dpi); the drawn flat in E♭ major (OpusChords music font in the text layer, a raised flat on the page); PREPARATORY WORK in full capitals, regular weight; and the stacked 3 over 4 on listening p10. Cross-checked the words and fonts against the text layer. Typed the printed text of every in-scope field into a script (lead-in bullets as "\n• ", " • " between printed bullet lines, a space for unbulleted lines, tick boxes as "□ ") and compared each file string exactly (no normalisation needed: no doubled spaces), then listed the code point of every non-ASCII character in the file strings (¹ U+00B9, Ó, á, – U+2013, ’ U+2019, • U+2022, □ U+25A1, ♭ U+266D). Elective Q2-Q4(b) carry no grid stem (null fields skipped).
